title: What If London Had No Thames Barrier?

scenes.text: What if London had no Thames Barrier? Ten steel gates stand between the city and the sea.
In 1953, a surge killed 307 people in eastern England and flooded London's East End.
The barrier opened in 1984 to make sure that never happens again.
It now protects about 1.4 million people across 125 square kilometres of central London.
The homes behind it are worth around 321 billion pounds.
In its first 40 years, the gates were raised 221 times. Without them, London would need flood walls as tall as Victorian streetlamps.
